results.title: Senegal vs Iraq Prediction » Betting Tips
highlights:
Friday night in Toronto, 8:00pm kick-off at BMO Field, Senegal vs Iraq prediction. Senegal have built a reputation over the years as one of Africa’s most reliable tournament sides. Iraq, on the other hand, are back on the big stage for the first time in decades. It’s been a long road. In this Senegal vs Iraq preview, we’ll cover various angles to identify some solid betting tips.
[...]
Senegal still lean on that experienced core. Sadio Mané, now at Al-Nassr, remains the main man going forward. Even at this stage of his career, he’s the one you trust in big moments. He’s also the likely penalty taker, no surprises there. Behind him, Kalidou Koulibaly (Al-Hilal) brings leadership at the back, while Edouard Mendy (Al-Ahli) is still a steady presence in goal.
[...]
So, how do you approach this one? Senegal come in with serious momentum. They’ve been winning consistently, especially in big matches. Iraq have been solid too, but their games tend to be tighter, more cautious.
[...]
If you’re looking at general angles, Senegal to control the game feels like the obvious call. They’ve got more depth and experience at this level.
[...]
Honestly, it comes down to control and composure. Senegal are used to this stage. They’ve played against top teams, beaten big names, and handled pressure. Iraq are still finding their feet at this level.
[...]
That said, Iraq’s defensive discipline could make things awkward early on. You can imagine a slow start, maybe even a bit cagey. But over 90 minutes? Senegal should find a way through.
[...]
Match Prediction: Senegal to win. Bet with bet365.
[...]
A controlled Senegal win feels about right here. Something like 2-0 stands out. Not a blowout, but comfortable enough.
[...]
If Iraq nick something, it’ll likely come from a set piece or a quick break. But keeping Senegal out for long stretches is a tough ask.
[...]
This doesn’t scream high-scoring. Senegal are efficient rather than explosive, and Iraq tend to keep games tight.
[...]
Under 3.5 goals feels like the safer direction. Even under 2.5 isn’t a bad shout if you expect Iraq to sit deep and limit chances.
[...]

- Iraq have kept several clean sheets in recent qualifiers.
- This is the first-ever senior meeting between the two nations.
- Senegal have far more recent World Cup experience.
- Iraq are playing their first World Cup match in 40 years.
